biography.plain_text: John Spencer was a New Zealand industrialist whose family fortune came from Caxton Pulp & Paper. He inherited the business built by his father and grandfather, ran it before its sale to Carter Holt Harvey, and later held property and investment interests. He remained notably private despite his national business prominence.

long_biography.plain_text:
Paper manufacturer John Spencer sought a dependable timber supply for Caxton’s mill. He approached the New Zealand Forest Service about developing radiata pine for Caxton. When the agency considered the work outside its mandate, forester Peter Olsen left to establish his own company. Olsen arranged a lease of Māori-owned land for Caxton and his company began planting the forest that would supply its operations.

Spencer also helped connect a colleague with the company’s next owners. When Caxton was sold, he introduced accountant Liz Coutts to Carter Holt Harvey chairman Sir Richard Carter. Coutts subsequently became Caxton’s group financial controller and then chief executive.
